name: What’s the difference between an open-concept kitchen and a kitchen with a pass-through?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a full open-concept kitchen conversion and adding a pass-through opening?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a full open-concept kitchen conversion and adding a pass-through opening?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pass-through is a smaller change than a full open-concept conversion. It preserves more wall, more separation, and often more flexibility for storage, sound control, and hiding kitchen clutter. A full open-concept conversion removes the barrier itself and creates a continuous kitchen-living-dining space. That usually delivers the biggest visual impact, but it also requires more structural review, more finish work, and often more budget. A pass-through can be ideal when you want connection without fully exposing the kitchen. It is also a smart option in homes where the wall is structural, where the kitchen needs to remain somewhat separate, or where budget is limited. The right choice depends on how much openness you want, how much construction risk you can accept, and whether the kitchen will still function well once the boundary changes.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full open-concept conversion removes most or all of the separating wall and creates one shared space, while a pass-through keeps the kitchen mostly enclosed but opens a framed opening for light, communication, and serving food.
